payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Was the specific black DVD in the source image transformed so that the same DVD is visibly white in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass only if the source DVD can be confidently matched to an object in the edited image and that same object is visibly white rather than black; fail if the matched DVD remains black or the source DVD is absent without being transformed; unknown if the source DVD's identity or correspondence cannot be determined.
node.binding: Compare the source and edited images, tracking the requested black DVD by its visible shape, location, and surrounding scene context. Do not treat a newly appearing white disc as evidence that the source DVD was recolored; report unknown when correspondence is ambiguous.

node_traces.evidence: The source DVD appears as a small rectangular case or disc-like object near the center of the snow. In the edited image, two white circular discs are visible, but neither can be confidently matched to that source object by shape and scene context; the source object’s correspondence is ambiguous.

d2: The binding overweights uncertainty about whether the source item is truly a DVD and whether the edited disc is the same object. The source image shows a small rectangular, printed item near the center; the edit shows a white disc at that location, while a separate white disc appears on the dark object to the right. This is evidence of a likely transformation, but the trace does not establish which disc corresponds to the source item. Keep identity and correspondence as distinct checks: assess spatial/scene correspondence and visible change, and use unknown only when those cannot be resolved—not merely because the source is not unmistakably a DVD. Conversely, do not treat a nearby white disc alone as proof of a successful edit. The reference “no” is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth; the rubric’s “no progress” versus “partial progress” distinction may be ambiguous here, so inspect whether the node’s criterion captures requested progress rather than only post-edit DVD identity. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; this is a visual-evidence and criterion-resolution issue.

response.content: {"text":"Refine the binding to separate source-object identification, spatial correspondence, and color change. The source shows a small printed rectangular item on the snow near center; the edit has a white disc near that location and another white disc on the dark object to the right. Ask the evaluator to compare each candidate against the source using position and surrounding scene context, then judge whether the likely corresponding item visibly changed from black to white. Do not require the source to be unmistakably identifiable as a DVD, but do not count a nearby or newly appearing white disc as proof of recoloring. Reserve unknown for genuinely unresolved correspondence or visibility, rather than defaulting to it when the object’s label is uncertain. Also make the decision criterion align with the rubric’s distinction between no progress and partial progress: assess visible requested progress separately from complete fulfillment, without treating the aggregate reference label as atomic evidence. This is a visual-evidence/criterion issue; no transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported."}
